conflicts.kind: function without a part on the ESC pack node: V+ OR element
conflicts.description: The ADBMS1818's V+ must be at or above C18 - 0.3 V and C18 may not exceed V+ + 5.5 V. The always-on supply LTM8068EY#PBF gives 18 V on VOUT1 (stated as typical only; 17.7 V after an OR drop of 0.3 V): it misses the requirement for packs above 18.0 V (5 cells at 4.2 V) and C18 exceeds V+ + 5.5 V above 23.2 V (6 cells). V+ for 1 to 16 cells up to 67.2 V therefore needs an OR element from each tap that can be the pack top (V327): the pack-side branch drops at most 0.3 V at 1.4 mA from 0 to 50 degC and the supply-side branch blocks up to 67.2 V; 17 placements a board (need 85, gate 425 as single diodes). FU-2J returned no part: no candidate meets both V327's drop and V190's 10 uA at the top tap with the reverse leakage of up to 15 blocked branches (BAT46 parts sum to 35.6 to 39.6 uA at 25 degC; PMEG100T30ELP drops about 0.27 V at 1.4 mA at 25 degC but about 0.32 V at 0 degC and states no leakage between 25 and 85 degC). The function sits on the ESC pack node with no part in selection.json. A preload larger than 10 mA (stage 2) keeps the LTM8068 above its 15 mA minimum load.
conflicts.evidence: FU-2J/002-P2-R9.json reports 'V+ OR element: no part', 'V+ OR element placements and gate', 'LTM8068 minimum load and preload', 'LTM8068 VOUT1 tolerance'; FU-2J/010-adjudicator-R9.json and 011-adjudicator-R9-2.json (rulings); ADBMS1818 Rev. conflicts.kind: rail conflict: USB-C-powered logic supply exceeds the source current
conflicts.description: V91 (found, FU-2I): with neither the DC input nor the pack present, the shared USB-C connector powers the board through the BQ25723RSNR's VSYS. A 3 A, 5 V source gives 15 W x 94.7 % = 14.2 W at VSYS (13.3 W at the 2.8 A edge of the input limit). Loads with the servo converters off: 3.3 V rail 5.4 to 6.0 W, 5 V rail 10.8 W at the display's 2 A peak (8.2 W continuous), load-cell regulator 0.26 W: 16.5 to 17.0 W peak, 13.9 to 14.5 W continuous. The peak exceeds the source by 2.3 to 2.8 W and the continuous draw is at it. A 500 mA default source (2.5 W) cannot carry the 3.3 V rail. The LM61460's efficiency at 6.6 V in and the FUSB303B's 3.3 V draw are not read. Owner (V328, 2026-10-03): a current limitation; the display's 2.0 A peak is not supported from USB-C alone.

conflicts.description: The R5 row states it as a conflict if the display does not isolate its VBUS. FU-2I and FU-2F found (V80, Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-7 schematic) that the display's Type_C2 VBUS joins its 5 V net with only a TVS to ground, so link power from the TPS259474ARPWR reaches the VBUS pin of the display's native USB-C socket and back-feeds a host or charger plugged there. The IO board side blocks reverse current (V266), which does not stop the forward feed. Owner (V329, 2026-10-03): a current limitation; no host or charger on the display's native USB-C while the link cable carries 5 V; flashing the display and reading its console use that socket with the link cable removed.

conflicts.kind: SPI1_RX contention: the cell monitor barrier's reverse channel is not tri-stated
conflicts.description: GPIO 8 (SPI1_RX of the measurement coprocessor) is one net shared by the ADS1235IRHBR (CS GPIO 9), the MAX31856MUD+T (CS GPIO 13) and, across the barrier, the ADBMS1818ASWAZ-RL (CS GPIO 15). The ISO7741DWR's reverse channel OUTD (pin 6) drives a push-pull level whenever EN1 (pin 7) is high or open, and its input is the ADBMS1818's SDO, an open-drain output with a 5 kOhm pull-up that idles high, so with EN1 tied high OUTD drives GPIO 8 high continuously and fights the MISO output of the ADS1235 or the MAX31856 whenever either is selected; both release their output only when their chip select is high. EN1 is active high and the cell monitor chip select active low, so the drive is one inverter or one more GPIO from the 14 free (budgeted in GPIO: measurement as 35 of 48). FU-2J's P2 return stated 'enables tied high, no pin'; its adjudicator ruled that wrong (013) and left the check to P5. No page of the tree states the enable drive and selection.json names no part for it.

conflicts.kind: PIO budget omission: serial servo protocols on an output
conflicts.description: IOBoard.md (Outputs section, row 'Serial servo protocols out') and docs/Manifest.md:31 require S.BUS and other serial protocols on an output, 'one PIO program each' and 'one PIO program per serial protocol'. P5's main-chip PIO state machine budget (11 of 12), instruction memory budget (81 of 96 words), combinations and the 223-of-256 mix count contain no serial servo output, and P5 states neither a count for them nor an assumption. At the largest supported mix (all four ports bidirectional, socket and PPM) only 1 state machine (PIO0) and 15 words (PIO0) are free, so a serial servo output fits only as one state machine of at most 15 words bound after the others; with the socket as a PIO UART the number of such outputs the board supports is not stated. The count per protocol is not stated in the tree, so it is an assumption P5 has to state and add to the bind-order model. The earlier P5 critic raised the same omission (FU-2P56/003-P5-critic.json budget verdict 6) and the current return does not address it.

budgets.value: LTM8068EY#PBF, isolated (2 kVAC), referenced to the ESC pack negative, fed from a board rail that the pages do not state (VIN 3 to 27 V allows the 5 V or the 12 V rail; P5 bounds it on the 5 V rail): VOUT1 18 V (set by RFB1 2.37 kOhm, stated as typical only) with 1.4 mA of V+ load awake (IVP maximum) and 0.825 mA in standby, and the LDO output VOUT2 5 V at 31.0 mA awake at most (ADBMS1818 VREG 16.5 mA + isoSPI 8.1 mA + ISO7741DWR 6.4 mA; 35 mA peak with isoSPI traffic and conversions together) against 300 mA. VOUT1 supports about 80 mA at 18 V from a 5 V input (typical graph) against 42.4 mA awake with a 10 mA preload. The minimum load at VOUT1 18 V is about 15 mA at 25 degC (typical, higher when cold): with the monitor asleep and SPI idle (CSB and SCK high, SDO pulled up) the barrier draws 2.0 to 3.7 mA, so the asleep load is 12.0 to 13.7 mA with FU-2J's 10 mA preload, under 15 mA (adjudicator 011). The preload resistor is stage 2 and has to be larger than 10 mA, sized for the lowest operating temperature (not read); the awake budget leaves room (about 80 mA against 32.4 mA without it). The module's input draw at 18 V out is not read (the datasheet plots input current to 15 V out only); it is bounded at 0.2 A in the 5 V rail's sum.

budgets.reason: 31.0 mA = 16.5 + 8.1 + 6.4; 1.4 + 31.0 + 10 = 42.4 mA; 0.763 W awake reproduce. The asleep load is 2.0 to 3.7 mA + 10 mA = 12.0 to 13.7 mA, under the 15 mA typical minimum, so the stage 2 preload has to be at least 13.0 mA (more when cold); awake that is 45.4 mA against about 80 mA. The asleep case assumes 'SPI idle (CSB and SCK high)', but SCLK is shared with the ADS1235 and MAX31856: ADBMS1818 with ISOMD = V- wakes its SPI port on CSB or SCK activity (adbms1818.pdf lines 2133-2135), so the monitor leaves sleep whenever those ADCs run. This adds load and does not lower it; the minimum-load conclusion is unchanged.

assumptions.value: 2 PIO state machines on the measurement coprocessor, both in PIO1: 1 receive and 1 transmit, 13 instruction words (UART receive 9 + transmit 4, sized from the pico-examples UART programs, which are not in the tree); one receiver input on GPIO 23 (V68); the receive program takes the S.BUS 8E2 100 kbaud frame with the pad's input inversion, and the other buses (iBUS, SUMD, CRSF, SRXL2, JETI EX Bus) as UART; the transmit state machine drives GPIO 23 through SN74LVC1T45DBVR, whose direction pin takes 1 more GPIO (counted in GPIO: measurement). A hardware UART is available for the receive-only buses: UART1 is free on this chip and GPIO 23 has UART1_RX (funcsel 0x0b), but UART1_TX would need GPIO 20, 22, 24 or 26, which the encoder, a chip select and the TCA9548A reset hold, so the transmit direction needs PIO.
assumptions.why: No receiver PIO program is written (docs/Receivers.md); V71 (owner, 2026-09-28) says the bench transmits on a receiver input for JETI EX Bus and SRXL2; the map puts the receiver on PIO1; the count must be stated, and the count for transmit is the smallest that meets V71.
assumptions.source: hardware/docs/pinmap.json measurement GPIO 23; Research.md V68, V71; docs/Receivers.md:10-16 and shared/sbus/include/sbus.h:4-17 in checkout-7e74cd442a79; pico-sdk 2.3.0 io_bank0.h GPIO23 funcsel table; hardware/docs/Pins.md Not known (receive-only)
assumptions.reason: The tree states no receiver PIO program or count (IOBoard.md S.BUS input row: 'a PIO program that is not written'; V68 is for research; V71 says the bench transmits on a receiver input for JETI EX Bus and SRXL2). 2 state machines and 13 words match pico-examples uart_rx (9 words) and uart_tx (4 words), counted from the raw files in scratch/FU-2P56/P5-critic (uart_rx_mini is 4 words); GPIO 23 UART1_RX at funcsel 0x0b confirmed in io_bank0.h (pico-sdk 2.3.0 local copy). One correction to its supporting text: UART1_TX is also available on GPIO 36, 38, 40 and 42, free on this chip, so the claim that only GPIO 20, 22, 24 and 26 offer it is wrong; PIO for the shared half-duplex wire remains reasonable and the value assumed stands.

assumptions.value: 2 PIO state machines and 13 words (transmit 4 + receive 9, assumed) for a port in a programming mode, on the main coprocessor, bound before ports 1 to 4, the socket and PPM (V330): a port enters a programming mode with the port released; a mode change that cannot keep that order rebinds every output from scratch with the outputs stopped. With that order 223 of the 256 mixes bind, all 4 ports in programming mode take 11 of 12 state machines and 69 words, and 33 mixes are refused (see combinations). The one-wire bootloader (BLHeli_S and AM32, 19,200 baud, half duplex), the ESCape32 CLI and Hitec D-series run as PIO UART programs; VESC's 115,200 baud runs on UART1 (GPIO 4, 5, V67), not on a state machine. The measurement chip has none.
assumptions.why: No programmer protocol has run on a wire (STATUS.md, shared/ui/programmer_screen.c:237-248), the levels, form and baud of Hitec D-series and the ESCape32 baud are not stated (V59 to V62, V60 answered 'not known'), and each bound output loads its own copy of its program, so a count has to be assumed; pico-sdk 2.3.0 reserves nothing per port, which V330 answers with the bind order.

assumptions.value: 5 ms (a 200 Hz current sensor): the measurement coprocessor reads each INA3221 and checks the 3.0 A ceiling at every sample; the INA3221 refreshes its 3 channels in 3.63 ms at most in shunt-only mode, so each channel gives a fresh value at every 5 ms sample.
assumptions.why: The tree does not state the period of the coprocessor's port-current sample; docs/Servo.md:35 says 'checked at every sample' and the host test models the sensor at 5 ms. An earlier P5 assumed 20 ms, the BENCH sampling period, which its critic rejected: that period belongs to the motor monitor's BENCH reading.
assumptions.source: test/host/test_servo_limit.c:19 ('#define SAMPLE_MS 5u /* a 200 Hz current sensor */') and docs/Servo.md:35 in checkout-7e74cd442a79; FU-2I/002-P2-R8.json found V173 (read 2026-10-03T00:15:40Z); INA3221 SBOS576C conversion table (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ina3221.pdf, read 2026-10-03T12:35:42Z)
assumptions.reason: IOBoard.md states 'The range and sample rate each port monitor needs are not stated' and docs/Servo.md says only 'checked at every sample'; test/host/test_servo_limit.c:19 models SAMPLE_MS 5u as 'a 200 Hz current sensor'. 5 ms is sourced and reasonable: the INA3221 refreshes 3 channels in at most 3.63 ms in shunt-only mode and a bus A sweep reads in 1.38 ms. It is not the 20 ms BENCH period of the motor monitor.

item.kind: function without a part on the ESC pack node: V+ OR element
item.description: The ADBMS1818's V+ must be at or above C18 - 0.3 V and C18 may not exceed V+ + 5.5 V. The always-on supply LTM8068EY#PBF gives 18 V on VOUT1 (stated as typical only; 17.7 V after an OR drop of 0.3 V): it misses the requirement for packs above 18.0 V (5 cells at 4.2 V) and C18 exceeds V+ + 5.5 V above 23.2 V (6 cells). V+ for 1 to 16 cells up to 67.2 V therefore needs an OR element from each tap that can be the pack top (V327): the pack-side branch drops at most 0.3 V at 1.4 mA from 0 to 50 degC and the supply-side branch blocks up to 67.2 V; 17 placements a board (need 85, gate 425 as single diodes). FU-2J returned no part: no candidate meets both V327's drop and V190's 10 uA at the top tap with the reverse leakage of up to 15 blocked branches (BAT46 parts sum to 35.6 to 39.6 uA at 25 degC; PMEG100T30ELP drops about 0.27 V at 1.4 mA at 25 degC but about 0.32 V at 0 degC and states no leakage between 25 and 85 degC). The function sits on the ESC pack node with no part in selection.json. A preload larger than 10 mA (stage 2) keeps the LTM8068 above its 15 mA minimum load.
item.evidence: FU-2J/002-P2-R9.json reports 'V+ OR element: no part', 'V+ OR element placements and gate', 'LTM8068 minimum load and preload', 'LTM8068 VOUT1 tolerance'; FU-2J/010-adjudicator-R9.json and 011-adjudicator-R9-2.json (rulings); ADBMS1818 Rev. item.kind: rail conflict: USB-C-powered logic supply exceeds the source current
item.description: V91 (found, FU-2I): with neither the DC input nor the pack present, the shared USB-C connector powers the board through the BQ25723RSNR's VSYS. A 3 A, 5 V source gives 15 W x 94.7 % = 14.2 W at VSYS (13.3 W at the 2.8 A edge of the input limit). Loads with the servo converters off: 3.3 V rail 5.4 to 6.0 W, 5 V rail 10.8 W at the display's 2 A peak (8.2 W continuous), load-cell regulator 0.26 W: 16.5 to 17.0 W peak, 13.9 to 14.5 W continuous. The peak exceeds the source by 2.3 to 2.8 W and the continuous draw is at it. A 500 mA default source (2.5 W) cannot carry the 3.3 V rail. The LM61460's efficiency at 6.6 V in and the FUSB303B's 3.3 V draw are not read. Owner (V328, 2026-10-03): a current limitation; the display's 2.0 A peak is not supported from USB-C alone.

item.description: The R5 row states it as a conflict if the display does not isolate its VBUS. FU-2I and FU-2F found (V80, Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-7 schematic) that the display's Type_C2 VBUS joins its 5 V net with only a TVS to ground, so link power from the TPS259474ARPWR reaches the VBUS pin of the display's native USB-C socket and back-feeds a host or charger plugged there. The IO board side blocks reverse current (V266), which does not stop the forward feed. Owner (V329, 2026-10-03): a current limitation; no host or charger on the display's native USB-C while the link cable carries 5 V; flashing the display and reading its console use that socket with the link cable removed.

item.kind: SPI1_RX contention: the cell monitor barrier's reverse channel is not tri-stated
item.description: GPIO 8 (SPI1_RX of the measurement coprocessor) is one net shared by the ADS1235IRHBR (CS GPIO 9), the MAX31856MUD+T (CS GPIO 13) and, across the barrier, the ADBMS1818ASWAZ-RL (CS GPIO 15). The ISO7741DWR's reverse channel OUTD (pin 6) drives a push-pull level whenever EN1 (pin 7) is high or open, and its input is the ADBMS1818's SDO, an open-drain output with a 5 kOhm pull-up that idles high, so with EN1 tied high OUTD drives GPIO 8 high continuously and fights the MISO output of the ADS1235 or the MAX31856 whenever either is selected; both release their output only when their chip select is high. EN1 is active high and the cell monitor chip select active low, so the drive is one inverter or one more GPIO from the 14 free (budgeted in GPIO: measurement as 35 of 48). FU-2J's P2 return stated 'enables tied high, no pin'; its adjudicator ruled that wrong (013) and left the check to P5. No page of the tree states the enable drive and selection.json names no part for it.
item.evidence: FU-2J/013-adjudicator-R9-3.json; FU-2J/005-rerank-R9.json report 'Shared SPI1_RX line and the barrier's reverse channel'; FU-2J/009-P4-datasheet-R9.json; hardware/docs/Pins.md:105-112, :156-158, :173-176; ISO7741 SLLSEP4K (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/iso7741.pdf, read 2026-10-03T12:45:35Z); ADBMS1818 Rev. B pin description and SDO polling text (https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/adbms1818.pdf, read 2026-10-03T12:45:51Z); ADS1235 SBAS824 (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ads1235.pdf) and MAX31856 19-7534 (https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/max31856.pdf), both read 2026-10-03T12:45:35Z

item.kind: PIO budget omission: serial servo protocols on an output
item.description: IOBoard.md (Outputs section, row 'Serial servo protocols out') and docs/Manifest.md:31 require S.BUS and other serial protocols on an output, 'one PIO program each' and 'one PIO program per serial protocol'. P5's main-chip PIO state machine budget (11 of 12), instruction memory budget (81 of 96 words), combinations and the 223-of-256 mix count contain no serial servo output, and P5 states neither a count for them nor an assumption. At the largest supported mix (all four ports bidirectional, socket and PPM) only 1 state machine (PIO0) and 15 words (PIO0) are free, so a serial servo output fits only as one state machine of at most 15 words bound after the others; with the socket as a PIO UART the number of such outputs the board supports is not stated. The count per protocol is not stated in the tree, so it is an assumption P5 has to state and add to the bind-order model. The earlier P5 critic raised the same omission (FU-2P56/003-P5-critic.json budget verdict 6) and the current return does not address it.
item.evidence: hardware/docs/IOBoard.md rows 'Serial servo protocols out', 'PIO state machines', 'PIO instruction memory' (checkout 7e74cd442a79, read 2026-10-03T13:1xZ); docs/Manifest.md:31 ('one PIO program per serial protocol'); shared/link/include/link_pages.h:134-151 (no driver number for serial protocols); critic model /home/claude/rcbench-research/round2/scratch/FU-2Q/P5-critic/enum.py (all-bidirectional mix 11 state machines, 81 words, run 2026-10-03T13:22:13Z); FU-2P56/003-P5-critic.json

conflicts.kind: rail conflict: pack path drop allowance and pack protection window
conflicts.description: V294 allows 0.2 V from the cells to the converters at 52.1 A (3.84 mOhm for the protector MOSFETs, ideal-diode MOSFETs, 1 mOhm shunt, XT60 and wiring). The BQ25723RSNR's battery sense resistor RSR, 5 mOhm and in the pack-to-load path, alone drops 0.261 V and dissipates 13.6 W at 52.1 A, 0.313 V with the BQ40Z80RSMR's 1 mOhm shunt, before the BATFET, the MOSFETs and the connector. At the 6.0 V sizing corner the recomputed pack current is 54.0 A with 6 mOhm in the path (52.5 A at 3 mOhm, 56.4 A at 10 mOhm), above the BQ40Z80's untrimmed lower overcurrent edge of 52.21 A and, beyond 8.6 mOhm, above the post-trim edge of 55.25 A. At the 100.68 A upper short-circuit edge the RSR carries 0.503 V, 3 mV over the BQ25723's 0.5 V SRP-SRN absolute maximum, for up to 915 microseconds. Whether one P-channel BATFET carries 52.1 A is not known. Owner (V325, 2026-10-03): the pack path is judged at the 6.6 V floor, where the current is 47.5 to 50.3 A for 3 to 10 mOhm, inside both windows and under the 60 A rating; the drop, the 13.6 W and the 3 mV are current limitations; the converters' inductor clamps (ILIM_AVG 7 A minimum, 8 A typical, no maximum) keep the draw at 31 to 35 A from 6.0 V. The cell's 90 A continuous rating holds.

conflicts.kind: SPI1_RX contention: the cell monitor barrier's reverse channel is not tri-stated
conflicts.description: GPIO 8 (SPI1_RX of the measurement coprocessor) is one net shared by the ADS1235IRHBR (CS GPIO 9), the MAX31856MUD+T (CS GPIO 13) and, across the barrier, the ADBMS1818ASWAZ-RL (CS GPIO 15). The ISO7741DWR's reverse channel OUTD (pin 6) drives a push-pull level whenever EN1 (pin 7) is high or open, and its input is the ADBMS1818's SDO, an open-drain output with a 5 kOhm pull-up that idles high, so with EN1 tied high OUTD drives GPIO 8 high continuously and fights the MISO output of the ADS1235 or the MAX31856 whenever either is selected; both release their output only when their chip select is high. EN1 is active high and the cell monitor chip select active low, so the drive is one inverter or one more GPIO from the 14 free (budgeted in GPIO: measurement as 35 of 48). FU-2J's P2 return stated 'enables tied high, no pin'; its adjudicator ruled that wrong (013) and left the check to P5. No page of the tree states the enable drive and selection.json names no part for it.

Per transaction: MCP23017 write 29 SCL cycles, 0.073 ms at 400 kHz (0.29 ms at 100 kHz); two-byte read 0.12 ms (0.48 ms); BQ40Z80 word read with PEC about 0.57 ms at 100 kHz. A 396-byte output-binding record to the FRAM is 3,591 SCL cycles: 8.98 ms at 400 kHz, 35.9 ms at 100 kHz (FU-C1); the EEPROM alternative is 7 page writes of 603 cycles plus 5 ms tW each: 10.6 ms of bus time, 45.6 ms per save. A port enable queued behind a save waits at most 9 ms (36 ms at 100 kHz), against the 80 ms and 100 ms windows. Port switches open on the expander reset (GPIO 14) within microseconds, not over I2C (V127: 5 ms). Poll load: expander read-back every 10 ms is 3.6 % of the bus at 400 kHz. Within.

budgets.value: Path of V160 (owner, 2026-10-03): the coprocessor's overcurrent or over-temperature action latches its failsafe; it then refuses (NACKs) the panel's control writes; the panel stops its heartbeat; the monostable opens the ESC pack switches. No processor, register or firmware enters the path from GPIO6 to a gate, and the TPSI3052DWZR drivers take the latch output alone (V53). Detection: the INA228 compares the averaged result (SLOWALERT 1, 1052 us shunt and bus, AVG 4): one result every 8.42 ms (8.50 ms at -1 %), ALERT within 2 results, 17.0 ms of the crossing; SOVL 30.00 mV = 150 A on 200 uOhm and 300 A on 100 uOhm; one 74VHC21FT gate (8.5 ns) to a main interrupt; disarm on the next 1 ms pass (IOBoard.md: ALERT within 20 ms). Panel side, from firmware/panel/main/main.c at 7e74cd442a79: poll_far_end runs a poll every 50 ms while the link is up (:3490); poll_bench sends the control write while the panel is armed, and a NACK reply to it calls arming_stop_from_far_end (:3188-3203), which makes arming_heartbeat false; beat() then drives the heartbeat low in the next 5 ms control pass (:716), and that edge starts the monostable's 155 to 185 ms. Sum from the crossing: 17 (INA228 ALERT) + 20 (IOBoard.md's 20 ms to the disarm, counted beside the 17 as FU-2P56 did) + 50 (poll) + 5 (read and write exchanges, assumed; not stated) + 5 (control pass) + 185 (monostable) + 5 (switch) = 287 ms against the 500 ms stop deadline (V1, V159, V288): 213 ms margin; FU-2P56's sum without the last two panel terms was 277 ms. Over-temperature, from detection (two consecutive conversions above the limit, V288) the same 270 ms applies; from the crossing the MCP9808 at the onboard shunt adds 195 ms at 0.25 degC (65 ms a conversion typical, no maximum stated; 750 ms at the default 0.0625 degC, so firmware writes the resolution register). Two limits stand: the action is not built in the coprocessor's firmware (V160), and the panel sees the NACK only while it is armed and polling.

budgets.value: Reset supervisor TPS3703A7330DSERQ1 (F12): undervoltage 3.046 to 3.092 V, release at most 3.117 V, delay tD 7 to 13 ms with CT open (TPS3703A), overvoltage at least 3.508 V, startup delay 300 us. 3.3 V regulator LMQ66430MC3RXBRQ1: output 3.27 to 3.32 V (3.237 to 3.353 V with ripple and transient, inside 3.201 to 3.399 V); tSS is the time from the first switching pulse to 90 % of the set point, 2 / 3.5 / 4.6 ms (minimum, typical, maximum), after an enable delay of about 2.5 ms. The supervisor's delay counts from the rail crossing its release threshold, 3.117 V, which is 94.5 % of 3.3 V: on a linear ramp the rail crosses at 4.83 ms and reaches its final value 0.28 ms later (4.6 ms / 0.9 = 5.1 ms from the first pulse), so the release comes at least 7 ms after the crossing and at least 6.7 ms after regulation; the enable delay shifts both. The clear releases only inside the band. The band between 3.117 V and 3.201 V, where the window is not specified, is crossed during the ramp inside the 7 ms delay; in a dip that stays above the undervoltage threshold it is not closed (R3's open point). The 5 V rail LM61460AFSQRJRRQ1 tSS 3.5 / 5 / 7 ms; either order is accepted (V106; TCAN1472 passive unpowered). The latch's TLV803SDBZR holds every rail latch set below 2.87 to 2.99 V until the first F11 clear. The ramp is assumed linear (the datasheet draws it without a figure). Within.

assumptions.value: 2 PIO state machines on the measurement coprocessor, both in PIO1: 1 receive and 1 transmit, 13 instruction words (UART receive 9 + transmit 4, sized from the pico-examples UART programs, which are not in the tree); one receiver input on GPIO 23 (V68); the receive program takes the S.BUS 8E2 100 kbaud frame with the pad's input inversion, and the other buses (iBUS, SUMD, CRSF, SRXL2, JETI EX Bus) as UART; the transmit state machine drives GPIO 23 through SN74LVC1T45DBVR, whose direction pin takes 1 more GPIO (counted in GPIO: measurement). A hardware UART is available for the receive-only buses: UART1 is free on this chip and GPIO 23 has UART1_RX (funcsel 0x0b), but UART1_TX would need GPIO 20, 22, 24 or 26, which the encoder, a chip select and the TCA9548A reset hold, so the transmit direction needs PIO.
assumptions.why: No receiver PIO program is written (docs/Receivers.md); V71 (owner, 2026-09-28) says the bench transmits on a receiver input for JETI EX Bus and SRXL2; the map puts the receiver on PIO1; the count must be stated, and the count for transmit is the smallest that meets V71.
